cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here would be about sweep TIMING rather than about the defect.

title: a line buffer was freed at entry and republished only on the success path
object: the metadata line buffer, one getline() allocation stored in c->line
lifetime_ender: free(c->line) at entry, which does not clear the field
shape: a free-at-entry whose republish happens on only one of four return paths
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct malloc/calloc/getline allocation, with neither memcached suballocator in the path.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is the NEXT call's entry free, of the same pointer.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: 1.6.45:restart.c carries `c->line = NULL;` beside the entry free (`grep -c` = 1). The form without it is at 0d4901071c74^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.
nested_why: the object came straight from malloc / calloc / getline, with neither slabs.c nor cache.c between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../allocator-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the free is at the TOP of the function and the republish at the bottom, so the three return paths between them -- NOTAG, BADLINE and DONE -- all leave the field dangling. The fix clears it beside the free rather than adding a republish to each path, which is what makes the function safe to re-enter however it returned.
